headline: Cyclicals Lead a Choppy Rally as Hormuz Tensions Keep Markets on Edge
body_html:
Tuesday's session closed with a modest advance in breadth — 315 names finishing higher against 230 lower across the 549-stock universe — but the headline number obscured a complicated day driven almost entirely by geopolitical whiplash. Early optimism over a possible U.S.-Iran diplomatic opening lifted oil prices and sent rate-sensitive cyclicals surging; by afternoon, an Iranian security-council statement warning that the Strait of Hormuz would remain closed absent U.S. concessions knocked the wind out of the rally's more speculative edges.

The sector rotation told the real story. Homebuilders topped the tape with a gain of 2.07%, followed by semiconductors at 1.45% and energy at 1.06% — a trio of rate, tech, and commodity plays that suggests investors were hedging multiple scenarios simultaneously. Materials added 0.86%. On the other side, consumer names fell 0.70%, software shed 0.29%, and healthcare was essentially flat at negative 0.02%, indicating that defensive and discretionary positioning was quietly unwound in favor of hard-asset and cycle-exposed names.

The standout mover of the day was Everpure, the storage-hardware company trading under the ticker P, which surged 11.64% to lead all gainers. Semi-equipment names Onto Innovation and FormFactor also posted sharp advances of 9.76% and 7.65%, respectively, reinforcing the session's tilt toward industrial and technology hardware. The session's clearest lesson: when geopolitics oscillate by the hour, the market votes with cyclicals and hedges with everything else.

briefs.headline: Hub Group Buckles Under the Weight of a Brutal Session
briefs.body: Freight carrier Hub Group was the day's most punishing decliner, shedding nearly 20% to close down 19.75%. The magnitude of the drop stood apart from all other losers and suggests company-specific news compounded any macro-driven freight-sector anxiety. The move made Hub Group an uncomfortable outlier in an otherwise broadly positive industrial tape.

briefs.headline: Iranian Officials Harden Stance on Hormuz Closure
briefs.body: An Iranian security-council spokesman reiterated Tuesday that the Strait of Hormuz will remain closed until Washington satisfies Tehran's stated conditions, effectively cooling the morning's diplomatic optimism. The statement reverberated across Gulf equity markets, where stocks fell sharply, and kept crude traders cautious even as oil prices held onto moderate gains on the day.

briefs.headline: Semi-Equipment Names Stage a Coordinated Advance
briefs.body: Onto Innovation and FormFactor rose 9.76% and 7.65%, respectively, making semiconductor equipment the most consistently rewarded pocket of the technology universe on Tuesday. The paired gains point to renewed confidence in capital-spending cycles for chip manufacturing, even as broader software names lagged and the consumer-technology space remained under pressure.

briefs.headline: AECOM and Middleby Drag on the Industrial Complex
briefs.body: While homebuilders and energy lifted the cyclical trade, two prominent industrial names moved sharply in the wrong direction. Engineering firm AECOM fell 8.53% and equipment maker Middleby dropped 7.91%, suggesting company-level disappointments were cutting against the sector's otherwise constructive tone and keeping the Industrials aggregate to a slim 0.27% advance.

briefs.headline: Cardinal Health Earns a Price-Target Increase on Profit Outlook
briefs.body: Analysts raised their price objective on Cardinal Health following the healthcare distributor's upbeat profit guidance, a bright spot in a sector that finished the session essentially flat at negative 0.02%. The upgrade underscores a divergence within healthcare: device and biotech names like Artivion and Sarepta Therapeutics posted solid individual gains even as the broader group tread water.

briefs.headline: Prediction Markets Eye a Busy Political Season Ahead
briefs.body: Polymarket, the online prediction-markets platform, is reportedly moving to strengthen its operational footing in anticipation of a surge in trading activity tied to the fall political calendar. The development highlights growing mainstream interest in event-driven markets as a real-time barometer of macro and political risk — a sentiment instrument increasingly watched alongside traditional volatility gauges.
